sections.title: Transaction Summary
sections.author: M
sections.text:
**Header fields**
Borrower: Larkspur Precision Components, Inc. [D2, header]. Request type: Amended and restated credit agreement with facility increase [D2, header; D5, ¶4]. Total commitment: $18.0M [D1, §3 note]. Underwriter: Not in provided documents: underwriter name; the credit file assignment record would normally contain it. Senior reviewer: Not in provided documents: senior reviewer name; the credit file assignment record would normally contain it. Date: Not in provided documents: memo date; the underwriter sets it.

**Request**
On 2026-08-19, Erik and Anders Halvorsen asked Meridian to increase the facility to $18.0 million. The increase funds a 60,000 sq ft Rockford plant expansion ($6.0 million) tied to a new multi-year Customer A program [D5, ¶4]. The approved $12.0 million facility ($7.0M term loan and $5.0M revolver) dates from June 2023 [D5, ¶2]. The borrower wants to close by November 30, 2026 so construction can start before winter [D5, ¶4]. The borrower said a national bank has offered to deliver a term sheet within 10 business days [D5, ¶4].

**Proposed Facility**
The proposed facility totals $18.0M: a $12.0M term loan and a $6.0M revolver [D1, §3 note]. The draft Amended and Restated Credit Agreement is dated Sept 22, 2026 [D2, header].

- **Term Loan.** Principal amount: $12,000,000 [D2, §2.1(a)]. The loan matures five years after the Closing Date and amortizes on a seven-year schedule, with the unpaid principal balance due at maturity [D2, §2.1(a)].
- **Revolving Commitment.** Aggregate principal outstanding may not exceed $6,000,000 [D2, §2.1(b)]. The commitment terminates, and all revolving loans are due, five years after the Closing Date [D2, §2.1(b)].

**Use of Proceeds**
Per the draft agreement, the Borrower may use Term Loan and revolving loan proceeds only to refinance the existing term loan owed to the Lender, fund the Expansion Project, and pay fees and expenses under the agreement [D2, §2.1(c)]. The spread allocates term loan proceeds as follows: refinance existing Meridian term loan (5,600), fund plant expansion (6,000), pay fees (400), total 12,000 [D1, §3 note].

**Security (summary; detail in Section 5)**
Obligations are secured by a first-priority security interest in all present and future Borrower assets, a first mortgage on the Rockford, Illinois plant, and a limited guaranty from Erik Halvorsen capped at $3,000,000 in the aggregate [D2, §2.2].

**Sources used:** D1 §3 note; D2 header, §2.1(a)-(c), §2.2; D5 ¶2, ¶4.

**Underwriter to complete:**
- Header fields: underwriter name, senior reviewer name and memo date. These are not in the provided documents.
- Closing Date: Not in provided documents: the Closing Date is a defined term in the full draft agreement, which is not provided.
- Expansion Project: Not in provided documents: the definition is in Schedule 1.1 of the draft agreement, which is not included in the excerpt [D2, §1.1].
- Pricing and fees: Not in provided documents: interest rate, margin, fee schedule and amortization amounts. The term sheet or full draft agreement would normally contain them.
- Use-of-proceeds wording: D2 §2.1(c) refers to proceeds of the Term Loan and the revolving loans [D2, §2.1(c)], while the sources and uses in D1 are stated for term loan proceeds only [D1, §3 note]. Confirm how the §2.1(c) uses are allocated between the two facilities.
- Policy items for Section 6: D4 sets a total commitment threshold of $15.0 million for senior underwriter review and Senior Loan Committee approval [D4, §4.2.3(a)]. Section 6 should address this; a human approves any exception.
- Competing offer: the term sheet statement comes from the borrower's account in a relationship note [D5, ¶4]. The underwriter decides whether and how to reflect it.

sections.title: Borrower Overview and Relationship History
sections.author: M
sections.text:
### 2.1 Company Profile

Larkspur Precision Components, Inc. is a privately held company founded in 1994 in Rockford, Illinois, by Erik and Maria Halvorsen [D5, ¶1]. It makes precision-machined components and welded assemblies for agricultural and construction equipment OEMs [D5, ¶1]. It operates one plant with about 310 employees [D5, ¶1]. The fiscal year ends December 31 [D1, header]. FY2023 to FY2025 statements were audited by Hartwell & Lo LLP, with unqualified opinions [D1, header].

### 2.2 Ownership and Management

Ownership is Erik Halvorsen 55%, Maria Halvorsen 25% and Anders Halvorsen (COO) 20% [D5, ¶1]. The draft agreement defines "Founders" as Erik Halvorsen and Maria Halvorsen [D2, §1.1]. On 2026-09-02, Erik Halvorsen (64) said he plans to hand the CEO role to Anders within three years [D5, ¶5]. The same note says the family has discussed "informally" selling a minority stake to a private equity firm, with no timeline and no LOI [D5, ¶5].

### 2.3 Relationship History

Larkspur has been a deposit and treasury management customer of Meridian since 2019 [D5, ¶2]. Average operating deposits were $4.1 million over the trailing 12 months to August 2026 [D5, ¶2]. In June 2023, Meridian approved a $12.0 million facility: a $7.0M term loan and a $5.0M revolver [D5, ¶2]. The prior memo recorded the purpose as refinancing existing bank debt and funding working capital [D3, Part B §1]. Relationship notes record the facility as paid as agreed with no past dues [D5, ¶2].

At FY2025, the Meridian term loan balance was 5,600 and the revolver balance was 3,200 [D1, §4].

### 2.4 Compliance and Waiver History

The Q4 2024 compliance certificate arrived 18 days late [D5, ¶3]. Credit Administration waived the reporting covenant (waiver W-25-0117) [D5, ¶3]. All later certificates arrived on time [D5, ¶3]. The FY2025 certificate, dated April 28, 2026, reported total leverage of 1.90x (maximum 3.50x) and DSCR of 1.61x (minimum 1.20x). The borrower was in compliance with both financial covenants [D1, §7].

### 2.5 Current Request

On the 2026-08-19 call, Erik and Anders Halvorsen asked to increase the facility to $18.0 million [D5, ¶4]. The purpose is a 60,000 sq ft expansion of the Rockford plant ($6.0 million), tied to a new multi-year Customer A program [D5, ¶4]. The borrower wants to close by November 30, 2026, so construction can start before winter [D5, ¶4]. The borrower said a national bank has offered to deliver a term sheet within 10 business days [D5, ¶4].

**Sources used:** D1 (header; §4; §7); D2 (§1.1); D3 (Part B §1); D5 (¶1, ¶2, ¶3, ¶4, ¶5).

**Underwriter to complete:**
- Not in provided documents: management biographies and tenure for Erik, Maria and Anders Halvorsen, and Maria's role in management. The borrower's management or KYC file would normally contain these.
- Not in provided documents: treasury management product details and deposit balances outside the trailing 12-month average to August 2026. The nCino product and deposit records would normally contain these.
- Not in provided documents: when the "informally" discussed private equity stake sale became known, and the size of the "minority stake." The D5 note gives no further detail.
- Legal review: §7.6 of the draft agreement makes it an Event of Default if the Founders cease to own "a meaningful portion of the voting equity interests" or cease to be "actively involved in the management of the Borrower" [D2, §7.6]. These terms are undefined in the excerpt. They are referred to the underwriter and legal, with the CEO transition [D5, ¶5] and possible minority sale [D5, ¶5] as relevant facts. Anders Halvorsen is not within the "Founders" definition [D2, §1.1; D5, ¶1].
- Policy item: D4 §4.2.4 requires the memo to address customer concentration in Section 7 where a single customer exceeds 25% of revenue. D1 §5 states Customer A's share of revenue. Flagged for Section 7, which is underwriter-authored.
- Possible CONFLICT for Section 3: FY2025 net income is 3,900 in the spread [D1, §1 Table 1: Net income, FY2025], while management commentary states "Net income rose to $4.2 million" [D1, §6]. Neither figure is used here, and I have not chosen between them.

sections.title: Financial Analysis
sections.author: M
sections.text:
### 3.1 Revenue and Earnings

Revenue was 61,400 in FY2023, 66,800 in FY2024 and 72,500 in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: Revenue, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025]. Revenue growth was 6.0% in FY2023, 8.8% in FY2024 and 8.5% in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: Revenue growth, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025].

EBITDA was 8,600 in FY2023, 9,500 in FY2024 and 10,400 in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: EBITDA, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025]. EBITDA margin was 14.0% in FY2023, 14.2% in FY2024 and 14.3% in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: EBITDA margin, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025].

Net income was 3,100 in FY2023 and 3,600 in FY2024 [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2023, FY2024]. **CONFLICT** on FY2025 net income: the spread shows 3,900 [D1, Table 1: Net income, FY2025], while the management commentary, as summarized by the analyst, states "Net income rose to $4.2 million" [D1, §6]. This draft does not choose between them.

Customer A accounted for 28% of FY2024 revenue and 31% of FY2025 revenue [D1, §5]. The top five customers accounted for 64% of FY2025 revenue [D1, §5].

FY2023 to FY2025 were audited by Hartwell & Lo LLP, with unqualified opinions [D1, header].

### 3.2 Leverage and Debt Service

Total funded debt was 22,400 in FY2023, 20,900 in FY2024 and 19,800 in FY2025 [D1, Table 2: Total funded debt, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025]. Total leverage was 2.60x in FY2023, 2.20x in FY2024 and 1.90x in FY2025 [D1, Table 2: Total leverage, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025].

FY2025 funded debt comprised the Meridian term loan 5,600, the Meridian revolver 3,200 and equipment notes from Prairie Equipment Finance 11,000 [D1, §4].

Debt service (P+I) was 4,500 in FY2023, 4,550 in FY2024 and 4,800 in FY2025 [D1, Table 1: Debt service (P+I), FY2023, FY2024, FY2025]. Unfunded capex was 1,200, 1,300 and 1,400, and cash taxes were 1,000, 1,150 and 1,250, for FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025 respectively [D1, Table 1: Unfunded capex; Cash taxes, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025]. DSCR was 1.42x in FY2023, 1.55x in FY2024 and 1.61x in FY2025 [D1, Table 2: DSCR, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025].

As spread, total leverage is total funded debt divided by EBITDA. DSCR is (EBITDA minus unfunded capex minus cash taxes) divided by debt service (P+I) [D1, §2: Definitions as spread].

The FY2025 compliance certificate, dated April 28, 2026, reported compliance with both financial covenants of the existing 2023 credit agreement: total leverage of 1.90x against a 3.50x maximum, and DSCR of 1.61x against a 1.20x minimum [D1, §7].

### 3.3 Liquidity

Cash was 2,100 in FY2023 and 2,600 in FY2024 [D1, Table 2: Cash, FY2023, FY2024]. Revolver availability was 1,800 in FY2023, 2,300 in FY2024 and 1,800 in FY2025 [D1, Table 2: Revolver availability, FY2023, FY2024, FY2025]. Liquidity (cash plus availability) was 3,900 in FY2023 and 4,900 in FY2024 [D1, Table 2: Liquidity (cash + availability), FY2023, FY2024].

Not in provided documents: FY2025 year-end cash balance and FY2025 liquidity. The spread export did not include them [D1, Table 2: Cash, FY2025; Liquidity, FY2025 and footnote *]. The borrower is to provide year-end bank statements with the Q3 2026 package [D1, §2: Footnote *].

Average operating deposits at Meridian were $4.1 million over the trailing 12 months to August 2026 [D5, ¶2].

### 3.4 Pro Forma for Proposed Facility

The proposed facility totals $18.0M: a $12.0M term loan and a $6.0M revolver [D1, §3: Note to Table 3]. The draft agreement provides a Term Loan of $12,000,000 and a Revolving Commitment not to exceed $6,000,000 [D2, §2.1(a), §2.1(b)].

On a FY2025 basis, pro forma total funded debt is 26,200, total leverage is 2.52x, debt service is 5,600 and DSCR is 1.38x [D1, Table 3: Total funded debt; Total leverage; Debt service; DSCR, Pro forma (FY2025 basis)].

Pro forma total funded debt of 26,200 comprises the proposed term loan 12,000, the Meridian revolver 3,200 and the equipment notes 11,000 [D1, §3: Note to Table 3]. Term loan proceeds refinance the existing Meridian term loan 5,600, fund the plant expansion 6,000 and pay fees 400, totaling 12,000 [D1, §3: Note to Table 3].

The draft agreement sets a maximum Total Leverage Ratio of 3.25 to 1.00, stepping to 3.00 to 1.00 for each fiscal quarter ending on or after December 31, 2027 [D2, §7.1]. It sets a minimum Debt Service Coverage Ratio of 1.25 to 1.00 [D2, §7.2].

Spread and draft agreement definitions differ in wording. The spread uses "unfunded capex" and "debt service (P+I)" [D1, §2: Definitions as spread]. The draft agreement uses "Unfinanced Capital Expenditures" and "scheduled payments of principal and interest on Total Funded Debt" [D2, §1.1]. The draft agreement tests the ratios quarterly on a four-quarter basis [D2, §1.1: "Total Leverage Ratio"; "Debt Service Coverage Ratio"]. The documents do not state whether spread figures equal the agreement's defined-term calculations. Referred to the underwriter.

### 3.5 Underwriter Commentary

Section 3.5 is underwriter-authored. Cited facts the underwriter may need:
- Customer A was 31% of FY2025 revenue [D1, §5]. Policy requires the memo to address concentration in Section 7 if any single customer exceeds 25% of revenue in the most recent fiscal year [D4, §4.2.4].
- Management expects the plant expansion to add capacity for the Customer A program beginning in 2027 [D1, §6].
- The Q4 2024 compliance certificate arrived 18 days late, and Credit Administration waived the reporting covenant (waiver W-25-0117) [D5, ¶3].
- Policy maximum for pro forma total leverage is 3.50x, and minimum for pro forma DSCR is 1.25x [D4, §4.2.1, §4.2.2]. Pro forma figures are in 3.4 above.

**Sources used:** D1 (header, §2, §3, §4, §5, §6, §7; Tables 1-3); D2 (§1.1, §2.1, §7.1, §7.2); D4 (§4.2.1, §4.2.2, §4.2.4); D5 (¶2, ¶3).

**Underwriter to complete:**
- CONFLICT: FY2025 net income is 3,900 [D1, Table 1] versus "$4.2 million" [D1, §6]. Resolve with the audited statements.
- Not in provided documents: FY2025 year-end cash and FY2025 liquidity. The Q3 2026 year-end bank statements would normally contain them [D1, §2: Footnote *].
- Definitional differences between the spread and the draft agreement (see 3.4). The "Expansion Project" definition is in Schedule 1.1, which is not provided [D2, §1.1].
- Section 3.5 Underwriter Commentary, reserved for the underwriter.
- Policy items for Section 6 and underwriter judgment: pro forma leverage and DSCR against D4 §4.2.1 and §4.2.2, total commitment against the $15.0M threshold in D4 §4.2.3, and the concentration disclosure in Section 7 under D4 §4.2.4.
